title: An invertible sheaf on a proper curve is ample exactly when its degree is positive
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes ampleness of an invertible sheaf on a proper curve by positivity of its degree. For the forward direction the proof uses that an ample sheaf has a power with a section whose nonvanishing locus is affine, that the curve is not affine, hence the section vanishes somewhere, so the degree of that power is positive, and multiplicativity of the degree gives positivity of the degree of L (proof lines 10005-10013). The converse uses that dim_k H^0(X, L^{tensor n}) is at least chi(X, L^n) = n deg(L) + chi(X, O_X), which grows linearly, so for any finite collection of closed points one can find sections separating them; this yields the ampleness criterion (proof lines 10016 onwards to line 10067). H2: the two directions each combine a degree computation with a section-existence argument, and the growth estimate is the key step of the converse.
